value.rationale: A recently resolved product-cycle convolution inequality motivates quantitative finite-modulus sharpening; Z/5 is the first odd cyclic group with two different nonconstant neighbor-average multiplier magnitudes. The exact nonlinear fourth-power coefficient differs strictly from the L2 spectral contraction, and the theorem fixes the full extremizing wave profile. Thus this is a natural sharp finite-state stability invariant useful to distinguish spectral from L4 mixing, rather than an arbitrary numerical slice.
